title: Editing a wastage % on the Order BOM destroys selectedCadId, fabricWidthInches and every generic trim FK — the DRAFT BOM in the DB has already been hit
claim: updateItems() DELETES all order_bom_items (line 2086) and recreates them (line 2099-2139) from the request body. The body is `updateOrderBOMSchema` → `orderBOMItemSchema` (backend/src/schemas/orderBom.schema.ts:35-63), which has NO field for `selectedCadId`, `fabricWidthInches`, or any of the 16 generic trim FKs the table actually stores (hookEyeId, snapButtonId, buckleId, beltId, velcroId, drawstringId, ribbonId, sequinId, beadId, motifId, interliningId, paddingId, otherFastenerId, otherTapeId, otherDecorativeId, otherFunctionalId — schema.prisma:219-238). Zod strips them, the createMany omits them, and they are written back as NULL. The trigger is not an obvious 'edit BOM' form: OrderBOMDetail.tsx:241-276 `handleWastageChange` fires on BLUR of the wastage input (line 698) and re-PUTs the ENTIRE items array. LIVE VICTIM, confirmed by query: of the 8 active order BOMs, ORD2026080032 v1 is the only DRAFT (the only status updateItems accepts) and the only one whose updatedAt (2026-08-29T10:30) is later than createdAt (2026-08-26T13:04). It is also the only BOM whose items all carry wastagePercent = 5.00 (every other BOM: 0.00). And it is the ONLY BOM with 0 rows carrying selectedCadId, 0 rows carrying fabricWidthInches, and an INTERLINING row ('Microdot Fusing') whose interliningId is NULL — while all 7 untouched BOMs, including ORD2026080033 v2 created 2026-08-29T10:28 (two minutes before), have selectedCadId set, fabricWidthInches = 52.00, and interliningId set on their Microdot Fusing row. Fields the schema DOES declare (greigeId, rateCardId, processorId, greigeCost 47.00, processingCost 10.00, buttonId) all survived on that same BOM — the loss maps exactly to the schema's field list. Response is `200 {message: 'Order BOM updated successfully'}`; nothing warns.
userImpact: 'Microdot Fusing' on ORD2026080032 now has no FK at all, so when that BOM is approved MRP will hit the `!material && !hasSpecificMaster` guard (mrp.service.ts:1315) and push it to skippedItems — the interlining silently drops out of procurement. The greige line lost its CAD link and width, so the Job Work Order loses fabric identity/width provenance (mrp.service.ts reads orderBomItem.selectedCad and fabricWidthInches) and the Change-Width feature loses its anchor. Every future wastage tweak on any DRAFT BOM re-inflicts this.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — every link traced in the current working tree, and the live-DB victim holds up under an adversarial alternative-cause check.

CODE CHAIN (all present today):
- `backend/src/routes/order-bom.routes.ts:64-68` — `PUT /:orderId/bom` runs `validateBody(updateOrderBOMSchema)`, so Zod STRIPS anything not declared.
- `backend/src/schemas/orderBom.schema.ts:34-63` — `orderBOMItemSchema` declares 26 fields. It has NO `selectedCadId`, NO `fabricWidthInches`, NO `cadAverageSnapshot`, and none of the 16 generic trim FKs (`interliningId`, `hookEyeId`, `snapButtonId`, `buckleId`, `beltId`, `velcroId`, `drawstringId`, `ribbonId`, `sequinId`, `beadId`, `motifId`, `paddingId`, `otherFastenerId`, `otherTapeId`, `otherDecorativeId`, `otherFunctionalId`) that `schema.prisma:219-238` actually stores.
- `backend/src/controllers/order-bom.controller.ts:163-183` — passes the stripped body straight through, no merge with existing rows.
- `backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:2086` `deleteMany` → `2099-2139` `createMany` — full delete+recreate from the request body only. The `createMany` object literal (2105-2137) lists exactly the schema's fields; all 19 undeclared columns are therefore written back as NULL. Response is `200 {message: 'Order BOM updated successfully'}` — no warning, and the UI does an OPTIMISTIC local patch (`OrderBOMDetail.tsx:278-287`) rather than refetching, so the wiped columns never even come back into view.

TRIGGER IS WORSE THAN CLAIMED: `OrderBOMDetail.tsx:698` is `onBlur={(e) => handleWastageChange(item.id, Number(e.target.value))}` with NO dirty-check anywhere in `handleWastageChange` (240-289). Tabbing through / clicking into and out of the wastage cell without changing anything re-PUTs the whole items array. `updateOrderBOM` has exactly one caller in the entire frontend — this one.

LIVE DB PROOF (read-only queries against the live DB). `ORD2026080032` v1, the only DRAFT BOM (`updateItems` refuses anything else — service:2068), createdAt 2026-08-26T13:04, updatedAt 2026-08-29T10:30:56:
- Its 9 items: `selectedCadId` NULL on all, `fabricWidthInches` NULL on all, and the `INTERLINING` row "Microdot Fusing" has `interliningId` NULL.
- Its SOURCE cost sheet `CS-1787635366491-a6akz3p` HAS the data: `style_costing_fabric_items.fabricCADId = 098d42c5-…`, `width = 52`, and `style_costing_trim_items` "Microdot Fusing" `interliningId = 3e1497cd-…`. Those cost-sheet rows have createdAt = updatedAt = 2026-08-25T09:01 — written BEFORE the BOM was created and never touched since, so "the cost sheet was edited afterwards" is ruled out.
- The create path has passed these through since well before 08-26: `git log -S` dates the `selectedCadId: fabricItem.fabricCADId` line (service:1146-1147) to 2026-03-24 and `interliningId: trim.interliningId` (service:838/967) to 2026-08-11. So the row MUST have been created with them.
- Control: `ORD2026080033` v2 (created 08-29 10:28, two minutes earlier, never edited) has `selectedCadId = adab35a3-…`, `fabricWidthInches = 52`, and `interliningId = 3e1497cd-…` (the identical master) on its Microdot Fusing row.
- The loss maps exactly to the Zod field list: on the same wiped BOM, `buttonId` (e2f54762), `greigeId`, `rateCardId`, `processorId` — all DECLARED in the schema — survived.
- No alternative writer explains it. The only other `order_bom_items` mutations are `mrp.service.ts:1279/1302` (sets `fabricId`/`laceId` only), `order-bom.service.ts:3031` (`syncBomFabricId`, sets `fabricId` only), and `order.service.ts:993` (full order delete). None NULLs these columns.
- All four `*_DEFAULT_WASTAGE_PERCENT` system settings are "0", yet every one of the 9 items carries wastagePercent = 5.00 while every other BOM in the DB is 0.00 — independent corroboration that this BOM went through the wastage path.

NOT GUARDED, NOT BASELINED: I grepped every `scripts/hooks/*-baseline.json` for order-bom/orderBom/order_bom — zero hits. The "Schema↔service update parity" smart-check only catches the inverse direction (Zod field missing from the service's update data), so this class is invisible to it.

DOWNSTREAM MONEY/QUANTITY IMPACT (all reached after the DRAFT is approved, i.e. AFTER the wipe):
- `mrp.service.ts:1868/1914/1951` — `fabricWidth: bomItem.fabricWidthInches` and `cadId: bomItem.selectedCadId` become undefined on the created `material_requirements`, so the PO/GRN carries no width (split-PO and width traceability gone), and `mrp.service.ts:1445 vs 1495` silently switches FABRIC stock netting from width-filtered to any-width.
- `mrp.service.ts:1888` — `bomItem.selectedCad?.processingBatchGroupColorId` is null, so the PROCESSING requirement loses its batch-group consolidation key.
- Worst: `mrp.service.ts:1195` `hasSpecificMaster` is computed from the trim FKs. With `interliningId` NULL and `materialId` NULL, the INTERLINING line hits the skip at `mrp.service.ts:1314` and DISAPPEARS from procurement entirely — reported to the user with the invented default reason "No material linkage (needs materialId, fabricId, laceId, greigeId, or a trim master ID)" while the cost sheet plainly has the linkage. Same misleading-reason signature as the lace bug.

TWO SMALL OVERSTATEMENTS in the claim, neither material: (a) it says `threadId` survived — on this BOM `threadId` is actually NULL, but that row is "Thread (Auto-added)" from a different creation path (the excluded THR-DEFAULT issue), not this wipe; (b) it says the loss needs "editing a wastage %" — a bare focus+blur is enough.
verdict.fix:
Stop rebuilding rows from a partial payload. Preferred fix in `backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:2084-2145`: replace the `deleteMany`+`createMany` with per-item `tx.order_bom_items.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { ...only the fields this endpoint owns } })`, keyed on the `id` the schema already accepts (`orderBom.schema.ts:36`), so no column can be lost by omission; reject/ignore items whose `id` doesn't belong to the BOM, and only fall back to create for items with no `id`. Given the sole caller edits one number, the smallest correct endpoint is a targeted "set wastage" that writes `wastagePercent`/`totalWithWastage`/`totalCost` for one item id.

If the delete+recreate must stay, then BOTH: (1) add `selectedCadId`, `fabricWidthInches`, `cadAverageSnapshot` and all 16 generic trim FKs (`hookEyeId`, `snapButtonId`, `buckleId`, `beltId`, `velcroId`, `drawstringId`, `ribbonId`, `sequinId`, `beadId`, `motifId`, `interliningId`, `paddingId`, `otherFastenerId`, `otherTapeId`, `otherDecorativeId`, `otherFunctionalId`) to `orderBOMItemSchema` and to the `createMany` map at service:2105-2137; and (2) have `handleWastageChange` (`frontend/src/pages/OrderBOMDetail.tsx:240-289`) echo them back — plus an early `if (clamped === Number(item.wastagePercent ?? 0)) return;` so a bare blur doesn't fire a write at all.

Repair the existing victim: BOM `ca957834-4b56-43b4-9823-5e06a9344584` (ORD2026080032 v1, DRAFT) must be regenerated from cost sheet `CS-1787635366491-a6akz3p` before it is approved — otherwise its Microdot Fusing interlining will be dropped from MRP and its greige requirement will carry no 52" width.

Guardrail (matches the repo's smart-check habit): add a detector asserting that any Zod item-schema feeding a delete-then-`createMany` on a table covers every non-generated column of that Prisma model — this is the inverse of the existing "Schema↔service update parity" check, which is exactly why this slipped through.

title: Cost-sheet Auto-Generate dedupes CAD rows by componentName, silently dropping a fully-costed second fabric — and the warnings array structurally cannot report it
claim: getCostSheetPreview builds `processedComponents` keyed on `cadRow.componentName || 'default'` (lines 184-193) and `continue`s on any later row with the same key, keeping only the most-recently-updated one. Two distinct style_fabrics rows attached to the SAME style component therefore collapse to one key (and every CAD row with a NULL componentName collapses to the shared key 'default'). The user-facing warning at lines 569-590 queries ONLY `totalCostPerMeter: null` rows, so a row that IS fully costed and was dropped by the dedupe can never appear in `warnings` — the response returns fabricDetails, fabricTotal and grandTotal as if that fabric did not exist. Live and reachable: replaying this exact dedupe over the DB's COSTING rows finds 8 affected styles. EBWW-007 has two APPROVED costed CAD rows, both componentName NULL, on two different style_fabrics (18e9bdcc… and 0030b9b6…) of the same component 'Shirt': 0.4967 m @ ₹63.09 and 0.9817 m @ ₹63.09. Auto-Generate keeps only 0.4967 m (₹31.34/pc) and drops ₹61.94/pc with warnings = []. That both rows are genuinely needed is proved by the saved sheet itself: style_costing_fabric_items for CS-1787831451033-1bz0htf contains BOTH lines. Same picture on EBWW-006 ('Shirt': keeps ₹25.71/pc, drops ₹58.77/pc), ESSKY084LS ('Shirt': keeps ₹25.24/pc, drops ₹51.31/pc), EBWW002, EBWW003, EBWW004, EBWW-009, EBWW-010.
userImpact: Auto-generated cost sheets understate fabric cost by roughly two-thirds on these styles (EBWW-007: ₹31.34 vs the real ₹93.28 per piece), and the omission is invisible — no line, no count, no warning. On a 2,500-piece order that is ~₹155,000 of fabric cost missing from the quote, which flows straight into the margin, the selling price and later into the Order BOM built from that sheet.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED end-to-end against the current tree and the live DB.

CODE CHAIN (all verified):
- backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:184-193 — `const processedComponents = new Set<string>()` keyed on `cadRow.componentName || 'default'`; :190-192 `continue`s on a repeat key. Rows arrive `orderBy: { updatedAt: 'desc' }` (:153), so the OLDER costed row is discarded. The same Set is reused by the RAW_MATERIAL_CALCULATION fallback loop at :257-264, so an RM row for the dropped fabric is skipped too.
- The function is `generateCostSheetFromStyle` (claim said `getCostSheetPreview`), reached via POST /api/style-costing/generate/:styleId (styleCosting.routes.ts:90). Naming slip only; the file:line is correct.
- :569-576 — the warnings query filters `totalCostPerMeter: null`, so a FULLY COSTED row dropped by the dedupe is excluded by construction. Claim's "structurally cannot report it" is exact.
- WORSE than claimed: frontend/src/services/costSheet.service.ts:131-134 returns `response.data.data`, while `warnings` sits at the TOP level of the response (:596) — so even the uncosted-row warning that does exist never reaches the UI at all.
- frontend/src/pages/CostSheetForm.tsx:1844 `setFabricDetails(generatedCostSheet.fabricDetails)` REPLACES the list. The style auto-populate path at :791-1024 walks every component x every fabric with NO dedupe, so a correct 2-row fabric list already on screen is overwritten by the 1-row deduped list; :1883-1886 then toasts "Pre-filled: 1 fabrics" as a SUCCESS message.

REACHABILITY OF THE UNGUARDED PATH: `selectedRunId` starts null (:145) and is reset to null on every style/mode change (:668, :707, :734); only a deliberate chip click sets it. The default click on the primary gradient "Auto-Generate from CAD" button (:2072-2083) therefore goes straight through the dedupe. The both-approvals gate at :89-129 passes for these styles (rows are approvalStatus=APPROVED AND costingApprovalStatus=APPROVED with a price), so nothing stops execution.

LIVE DB (read-only replay of the exact loop): 25 styles have costed COSTING CAD rows; 8 lose a fully-costed row, and in all 8 the dropped row is on a DIFFERENT styleFabricId than the kept one.
- EBWW-007 (f5007c83): kept a02d69aa sf 18e9bdcc 0.4967 m @ 50" ₹63.09; DROPPED 2b8a2d69 sf 0030b9b6 0.9817 m @ 52" ₹63.09. Both approvalStatus=APPROVED, costingApprovalStatus=APPROVED, isPreferred=true, same costing run e9574439, componentName NULL on both. Reported fabric cost ₹31.34/pc instead of ₹93.28/pc — 66% understatement — with warnings = [].
- Same on EBWW-006 (keeps ₹25.71, drops ₹58.77), ESSKY084LS (keeps ₹25.24, drops ₹51.31), EBWW002, EBWW003, EBWW004, EBWW-009, EBWW-010.

BOTH ROWS ARE GENUINELY REQUIRED — proved by the saved sheets: style_costing_fabric_items for CS-1787831451033-1bz0htf holds BOTH lines (fabricCADId a02d69aa and 2b8a2d69). Ditto CS-1787834589175-id4pc3v (EBWW-006) and CS-1787307376141-t5bnl76 (ESSKY084LS). EBWW002's two fabrics even sit on two DIFFERENT style_components, both with componentName NULL on the CAD row, so they still collapse to the shared 'default' key.

THE DEDUPE IS CURRENTLY PURE LOSS: zero (costingStyleId, styleFabricId) groups in the DB have more than one costed COSTING row, so it never suppresses a true costing-option alternate — it only ever discards distinct fabrics.

NOT ALREADY GUARDED / NOT BASELINED: no entry for style-costing-calc.controller.ts in any of the 26 scripts/hooks/*baseline*.json except two unrelated hardcoded-default keys (markupPercent: 15, valueLossPercent: 2). docs/bug-hunt/qty-rate-audit-findings-2026-08-24.json finding #104 mentions the same :183-193 de-dup, but its consequence is different (an unapproved re-costed clone becoming the style's cost basis); the "second distinct fabric silently dropped" consequence is catalogued nowhere.

WHY IT IS SILENT: HTTP 200; warnings [] by construction; the frontend discards warnings anyway; the success toast counts only what survived ("1 fabrics"), so a user who never counted rows before and after sees a green confirmation while a whole fabric — and 66% of the fabric cost — vanishes from the pricing document.

Only inaccuracies in the claim: the function name and the `continue` guard beginning at :190 rather than the block. Neither affects the substance. Severity critical stands: silent money corruption in the document that sets selling price, reachable today on 8 live styles.
verdict.fix:
Key the dedupe on fabric IDENTITY, not on the free-text, nullable component label, and make any drop reportable.

1) backend/src/controllers/style-costing-calc.controller.ts:187 (and the identical :258) — replace
     const componentKey = cadRow.componentName || 'default';
   with an identity key that cannot collide across distinct fabrics:
     const componentKey = cadRow.styleFabricId || cadRow.fabricId || cadRow.greigeId || cadRow.id;
   `cadRow.id` as the final fallback makes an unidentifiable row unique-to-itself, so it is never silently swallowed. (Verified safe: no (costingStyleId, styleFabricId) group in the DB currently has more than one costed COSTING row, so this suppresses nothing that is being suppressed usefully today. If option alternates per styleFabric are wanted later, pick within the group by `costingApprovalStatus in (APPROVED, ALTERNATE_APPROVED)` then `isPreferred` then `updatedAt desc` — never by componentName.)

2) Make the drop visible instead of invisible. In the loops, when a row is skipped by the dedupe, push it onto a `droppedCosted` list and add it to `warnings` at :585-590, e.g.
     `${droppedCosted.length} costed fabric row(s) were collapsed as duplicates and left out: ...`
   The existing warnings query at :569-576 must stay as-is (it covers uncosted rows) — this is a second, separate source.

3) Surface warnings at all. frontend/src/services/costSheet.service.ts:131-134 returns `response.data.data`, discarding the top-level `warnings`. Return `{ ...response.data.data, warnings: response.data.warnings }` (or the full envelope) and in frontend/src/pages/CostSheetForm.tsx:1883 emit `notify.warning(...)` for each warning instead of an unconditional success toast.

4) Optional hardening for the overwrite: at CostSheetForm.tsx:1844, if the incoming `fabricDetails.length` is less than the currently populated `fabricDetails.length`, confirm with the user before replacing rather than silently truncating.

Backfill note (out of scope for the fix, but the 8 affected styles — EBWW002/003/004/-006/-007/-009/-010 and ESSKY084LS — should be re-checked: any sheet regenerated via Auto-Generate rather than the run/style path will be carrying a single-fabric fabric cost).

title: Editing Order BOM wastage silently nulls trim master FKs and the fabric CAD link (confirmed on live data)
claim: `orderBOMItemSchema` (orderBom.schema.ts:34-63) declares 11 master FKs but omits the 16 generic-trim FKs (hookEyeId, snapButtonId, buckleId, beltId, velcroId, drawstringId, ribbonId, sequinId, beadId, motifId, interliningId, paddingId, otherFastenerId, otherTapeId, otherDecorativeId, otherFunctionalId) plus selectedCadId, fabricWidthInches and cadAverageSnapshot — all real order_bom_items columns that the CREATE path writes (order-bom.service.ts:828, 957, 1146-1147). validateBody strips anything undeclared, and `updateItems` (order-bom.service.ts:2086 deleteMany -> 2099 createMany) does not write them either, so they are NULLed. The frontend payload (OrderBOMDetail.tsx:246-273) also omits them. Trigger: a user tabs out of the inline Wastage % input (OrderBOMDetail.tsx:698 `onBlur={() => handleWastageChange(...)}`) on any DRAFT BOM — even re-entering the same number fires the full-items PUT. CONFIRMED LIVE: order_bom ca957834-4b56-43b4-9823-5e06a9344584 (createdAt 2026-08-26T13:04, updatedAt 2026-08-29T10:30) has an INTERLINING line 'Microdot Fusing' with interliningId=NULL and every other FK NULL, while all 7 sibling BOMs carry interliningId=3e1497cd-099c-4640-9429-5dd50fc12ade for the same component; its GREIGE line 'Shirt - Viscose Staple' lost selectedCadId and fabricWidthInches=52 that every sibling BOM still has. LABEL/BUTTON lines on the same BOM kept their FKs — exactly the columns the schema does declare. Silent because handleWastageChange does an optimistic local setBom() instead of refetching, so the page keeps rendering the pre-save values.
userImpact: The interlining line can no longer be resolved to a material: mrp.service.ts:1809-1816 pushes it into `skippedItems` with the invented reason 'Check material master linkages' and it never becomes a requirement or a PO — the fusing simply never gets bought, and the shortage only surfaces at cutting. The fabric line loses its CAD link, so mrp.service.ts:1869/1952 emits the requirement with cadId=undefined, detaching the buy from the width/marker it was planned against. Any BOM carrying one of the 16 generic trim types is one blur event away from this.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED, and slightly understated. Chain verified end to end in the current tree.

1) Schema strips: `orderBOMItemSchema` (backend/src/schemas/orderBom.schema.ts:34-63) declares 12 linkage fields and omits 19 real `order_bom_items` columns (prisma/schema.prisma:218-238): the 16 generic-trim FKs, `selectedCadId`, `fabricWidthInches`, `cadAverageSnapshot`. `validateBody` uses `schema.parse()` on a plain z.object (middleware/validation.middleware.ts:28), which strips undeclared keys — so even a fixed frontend payload would be dropped.

2) Service nulls them: `updateItems` does `deleteMany` (order-bom.service.ts:2086) then `createMany` (2099); the mapping block 2105-2137 never writes any of the 19 → NULL. The create path DOES write them (838, 967 for the generic trim FKs; 1146-1147 for fabricWidthInches/selectedCadId), so this is loss, not "never populated".

3) Frontend omits them and hides the loss: OrderBOMDetail.tsx:246-274 builds the payload without them; :698 `onBlur={() => handleWastageChange(...)}` fires the full-items PUT on any focus loss (React onBlur fires even with an unchanged value); :278-285 does an optimistic local `setBom` instead of refetching, so the page keeps rendering the pre-save objects. 200 OK, no toast, no visible change. It is the only caller of `updateOrderBOM` in the frontend.

4) Live DB proves it happened. `order_bom ca957834-4b56-43b4-9823-5e06a9344584`: sourceCostSheetId='CS-1787635366491-a6akz3p', copiedFromOrderId=NULL (so created by createFromCostSheet, which sets these columns), status DRAFT, isActive true, createdAt 2026-08-26T07:34 vs updatedAt 2026-08-29T05:00. Its INTERLINING 'Microdot Fusing' line has interliningId=NULL while 7 of the 8 other BOMs carry interliningId=3e1497cd-099c-4640-9429-5dd50fc12ade for the same component; its GREIGE 'Shirt - Viscose Staple' line has selectedCadId and fabricWidthInches NULL while 9 of 10 other fabric lines carry both. By elimination this is the only possible writer: every other order_bom.update site either flips status (approve 2205 / lock 2247) or isActive (supersede 1288/1520/1755, deactivate 2301, cleanup 2319, order.service.ts:721 cancel), and the row is still DRAFT + active. It is also the only DRAFT BOM in the database — a 1-of-1 hit rate on the reachable population.

5) Consequences are money/quantity, not cosmetic. An item with no resolvable FK is pushed to `skippedItems` and `continue`d in MRP (mrp.service.ts ~1345) — the interlining is dropped from the plan and never procured, and the reason surfaced blames the cost sheet ("No material linkage… select in cost sheet"). Losing fabricWidthInches routes the fabric line into the "any width" stock branch (mrp.service.ts:1495) instead of the ±0.5in width-matched branch (1445), so off-width stock nets against the requirement and suppresses a PO. Losing selectedCadId breaks the requirement→CAD provenance chain (mrp.service.ts:1869/1952; fabric-identity.helper.ts:10; cad-costing-provenance.helper.ts).

6) Not guarded, not grandfathered: no orderBom entry in schema-alignment-baseline.json, schema-service-parity-baseline.json, or schema-frontend-parity-baseline.json. The parity ratchets only detect Zod-declared fields missing from the service; the reverse direction (column written on create, absent from both Zod and the update block) has no detector. validateForMRP (order-bom.service.ts:2960-2984) does not inspect any of the 16 generic-trim FKs either, so it cannot catch this before MRP.

Two corrections. (a) `cadAverageSnapshot` is NULL on every order_bom_items row in the DB today (only createVersionWithWidthChange sets it), so that part of the loss is currently theoretical. (b) The claim understates scope: `copyFromPreviousOrder` (order-bom.service.ts:1471-1508) drops the same 16 trim FKs plus selectedCadId/fabricWidthInches when copying a BOM into a new order, and `createVersionWithWidthChange`'s unchanged-item branch (1709-1742) preserves the CAD fields but still drops the 16 trim FKs. Secondary: recreating rows with fresh uuids also NULLs material_requirements.orderBomItemId (optional relation, schema.prisma:3870, Prisma default SetNull), losing the price-provenance link read at mrp.service.ts:3624.

Critical: a passive UI interaction permanently corrupts the document that drives MRP and purchase orders, with zero feedback and a misleading downstream error.
verdict.fix:
Preferred (minimal + safest): stop rewriting rows wholesale. Only `wastagePercent` is user-editable on this screen, so replace the deleteMany/createMany in `updateItems` (backend/src/services/order-bom.service.ts:2084-2139) with a per-id `order_bom_items.update()` inside the transaction that touches only the fields the UI actually edits (wastagePercent, totalWithWastage, totalCost, plus quantityPerGarment/orderQuantity/unitPrice if editing is ever added), scoped by `where: { id: item.id, orderBomId: id }`. Reject or append items with no matching id rather than silently recreating. This preserves all 19 undeclared columns, keeps item ids stable (so material_requirements.orderBomItemId provenance survives), and needs no schema change.

Then send every line with `plannedQty > 0` and drop the `colorId &&` guard, keeping only `sizeId`.

3. Add a server-side reconciliation guard in `backend/src/controllers/dispatch.controller.ts:1136-1145`: when `skus` is a non-empty array, reject with a 400 if `skus.reduce((s,x)=>s+x.plannedQty,0) !== plannedDispatchQty`; and when the order has any breakup rows but `skus` is empty, reject rather than creating a headline-only ASN. That turns the current silent success into a visible error.

Also worth a smart-check rule (per the project's "every bug found → add a check" pattern): flag `.filter(...)` calls in submit handlers whose predicate tests an id field that is populated with `|| ''` elsewhere in the same file — that is exactly the shape of this bug and of the OrderForm size-matrix one.

title: Create ASN order picker filters on status 'CONFIRMED', which is not an OrderStatus — the 400 is swallowed and shown as "No orders found."
claim: The order search calls `getAllOrders({ search, limit: 20, status: 'CONFIRMED' })`. `status` is forwarded verbatim by frontend/src/services/order.service.ts:31, and GET /api/orders runs `validateQuery(orderQuerySchema)` where `status: OrderStatus.optional()` with OrderStatus = ['PENDING','IN_PRODUCTION','COMPLETED','DISPATCHED','CANCELLED'] (backend/src/schemas/order.schema.ts:10,86) — Prisma's OrderStatus enum has no CONFIRMED (schema.prisma:9361; the DB itself rejects the literal). Every request therefore returns 400 "Invalid query parameters". The useQuery has no onError and createQueryClient sets a global onError only for mutations (frontend/src/lib/query-client.ts:34-40), so nothing surfaces; the popover falls through to `<CommandEmpty>No orders found.</CommandEmpty>` (line 226). All 8 orders in the live DB are status PENDING, so the list would be non-empty if the filter were valid. It is silent because a validation failure is rendered as a legitimate empty result set.
userImpact: The "Create ASN" CTA on DispatchList (DispatchList.tsx:194) leads to a page where no order can ever be selected, and the screen tells the dispatch team there are no orders ready to ship rather than that the request failed — the ASN/booking step is unusable with no error anyone can report.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED — every link traced to real code, and the path is not merely reachable, it is the ONLY path.

1. Source. `C:\Users\NEW\garment-erp\frontend\src\pages\ASNCreateForm.tsx:57` — `queryFn: () => getAllOrders({ search: orderSearch, limit: 20, status: 'CONFIRMED' })`, `enabled: orderSearchOpen || !!orderSearch` (line 58), so simply opening the popover fires it. Grep confirms this is the only `status: 'CONFIRMED'` literal in `frontend/src`.

2. Forwarded verbatim. `frontend\src\services\order.service.ts:31` — `status: params?.status || undefined`; 'CONFIRMED' is truthy so it goes on the wire. No request interceptor in `frontend\src\lib\api.ts` strips or rewrites params (the decamelize block at lines 91-94 is commented out).

3. Server rejects. `backend\src\routes\order.routes.ts:49` — `router.get('/', validateQuery(orderQuerySchema), asyncHandler(getAllOrders))`, and it is the only GET '/' on the router (mounted at `/orders`, routes/index.ts:213). `backend\src\schemas\order.schema.ts:10` defines `OrderStatus = z.enum(['PENDING','IN_PRODUCTION','COMPLETED','DISPATCHED','CANCELLED'])`, used at line 86 as `status: OrderStatus.optional()`. I reproduced the parse with the repo's own zod 4.1.12: `CONFIRMED -> REJECT: ["Invalid option: expected one of PENDING|IN_PRODUCTION|COMPLETED|DISPATCHED|CANCELLED"]`, `PENDING -> PASS`. `validation.middleware.ts:72-78` turns that into `400 {error:'Validation Error', message:'Invalid query parameters'}` before the controller ever runs.

4. Prisma/DB agree there is no such value. `schema.prisma:9361-9368` = PENDING, IN_PRODUCTION, COMPLETED, DISPATCHED, CANCELLED, SPLIT. Live DB `enum_range(NULL::"OrderStatus")` returns exactly those six — the DB literally cannot hold 'CONFIRMED', so this is not a stale-schema artifact.

5. It is silent. The axios response interceptor (`api.ts:116-211`) only toasts for 401 / token-403; a 400 falls through to a bare `Promise.reject` at line 210. `query-client.ts:34-40` sets `onError` under `mutations` only, and grep shows no `QueryCache`/`queryCache` onError anywhere in `frontend/src`. The `useQuery` at ASNCreateForm:55 has no `onError`, no `isError` branch. So `ordersData` stays undefined → `const orders = ordersData?.data || []` (line 171) → the empty `CommandGroup` makes cmdk render `<CommandEmpty>{ordersLoading ? 'Searching...' : 'No orders found.'}</CommandEmpty>` (line 226). The user sees a brief "Searching…" (retry:2 in query-client means 3 attempts) and then a flat, authoritative "No orders found." A validation failure is rendered as a legitimate empty result set — exactly as claimed.

6. Reachability is stronger than the claim states. Live DB: 8 orders, all PENDING — so with a valid filter (or none) the picker would list 8 rows. And the claim understates the blast radius: I grepped every reference to `dispatch/asn` — the sole link into this page is `DispatchList.tsx:194` (`New ASN` button) with NO `?orderId=` query param. Nothing anywhere deep-links with `?orderId=`. Since the picker is the only way to set `selectedOrderId`, and `handleSubmit` hard-returns on `!selectedOrderId` (line 141), the entire Create-ASN flow is 100% uncompletable through the UI. `asn_applications` has 0 rows, consistent with a flow nobody has ever been able to finish.

7. Not already guarded, not baselined. The enum-drift ratchet (`scripts/hooks/drift-detectors.js:216-254`) scans backend `z.enum` declarations against Prisma enums — it has no visibility into a frontend string literal passed as an API param. Grep across all 25 `scripts/hooks/*-baseline.json` returns no mention of ASNCreateForm. No test covers it (`asn_applications` empty, no persistence-smoke entry).

Honest calibration caveats, since my default is skepticism: this is NOT data loss in the money/quantity sense of the two calibration bugs — nothing typed by the user is discarded on save, no number is corrupted, and business impact to date is zero because the feature has evidently never been usable. It belongs to the sibling class the mission names — "tells them something misleading" — where a failed request is dressed up as a valid empty answer. I keep it at major rather than minor because it is not an edge case: it fails 100% of the time on the only path into a shipped, sidebar-reachable create flow, and the misleading message ("No orders found") actively sends the user to look for a non-existent data problem instead of a code bug.
verdict.fix:
Two parts — the one-line correctness fix, and the reason it stayed invisible.

1. `frontend/src/pages/ASNCreateForm.tsx:57` — drop the bogus filter. 'CONFIRMED' is not an OrderStatus in any layer. Orders eligible for an ASN are the ones in production, so either omit `status` entirely:
   `queryFn: () => getAllOrders({ search: orderSearch, limit: 20 }),`
   or filter on a real value, e.g. `status: 'IN_PRODUCTION'`. Note that if you pick a single real status you will hide the 8 currently-PENDING orders, so omitting the filter (and letting the user search by order number) is the safer behaviour today. Also update the CardDescription at line 197 ("Choose a confirmed order…"), which is where the phantom 'CONFIRMED' concept leaked in from.

2. Surface the failure instead of rendering it as emptiness. Add `isError` to the destructure at line 55 and branch the empty state, so a failed fetch never again masquerades as "no results":
   `<CommandEmpty>{ordersLoading ? 'Searching...' : isError ? 'Could not load orders — please retry.' : 'No orders found.'}</CommandEmpty>`

3. Optional hardening for the bug class (this is the part guardrails missed): the enum-drift ratchet only compares backend Zod enums to Prisma enums. A cheap extension in `scripts/hooks/drift-detectors.js` — flag frontend `status: '<LITERAL>'` object properties passed into `services/*.service.ts` API wrappers when the literal is absent from the same-named Prisma enum — would have caught this at commit. Separately, `backend/src/schemas/order.schema.ts:10` is missing `SPLIT`, which Prisma's OrderStatus does have (schema.prisma:9367): any client filtering on SPLIT parent production runs gets the identical silent 400. Worth aligning in the same change, ideally by importing from `./generated/prisma-enums` per the /generate-zod-enums convention.

title: Cost-sheet update binds CAD rows to fabric rates by array position; the create path was already fixed to match by ID
claim: On cost-sheet UPDATE, style_costing_fabric_items are deleted (line 1208) and rebuilt by walking fabric_width_cad rows ordered by `updatedAt: 'desc'` (line 1055) and pairing the Nth unique CAD row with `fabricDetails[idx]` where `idx = fabricItemsToCreate.length` (lines 1068-1070) — a raw positional join between two unrelated orderings. The CREATE path in the same file (lines 315-357) does NOT do this: it was explicitly fixed ("P1.9: ID-based matching — fixes index-based mis-assignment when order differs") to match on fabricId, then greigeId, then fabricName, and only then fall back to index WITH a console.warn. That fix was never carried into the update path. Because `cadRows` is ordered by `updatedAt`, the pairing flips whenever a CAD/fabric-costing row is re-saved: re-costing the lining CAD row makes it sort first, so on the next cost-sheet save the shell fabric's average and rate get written onto the lining's CAD row and vice versa. The identity columns of the created item (fabricCADId, fabricId, greigeId, width) come from the CAD row while the money columns (cadMeters, costPerMeter, totalCost, fabricName) come from the mismatched JSON entry, so each row is internally inconsistent. Secondarily, `if (!jsonFabric) continue` at line 1070 never advances idx, so once fabricDetails is exhausted every remaining unique CAD row is dropped with no item and no warning. Reachable today: 30+ styles in the live DB have more than one unique CAD key (componentName|style_fabric_id|cutableWidth) feeding a cost sheet — e.g. style 730c69e4-b56f-4442-87fb-e86c78756845 has 4, and 5 more styles have 3. Current rows still pair correctly (the swap has not yet fired), so this is live-reachable rather than already-corrupt.
userImpact: The cost sheet's own total is unchanged by a swap — the same two rate x consumption products are still summed — so the sheet looks correct and nobody investigates. But order-bom.service.ts copies style_costing_fabric_items line by line into order_bom_items, which is what MRP and the greige/processing POs are priced and quantified from. A swapped pair means the greige PO for the lining is raised at the shell fabric's rate and metreage (e.g. Viscose Staple bought at Viscose Crepe's Rs 92.35/m and 1.30 m instead of Rs 63.09/m and 0.98 m), overpaying one weaver and under-buying the other, with the error only surfacing as a fabric shortage or a supplier invoice mismatch weeks later. The drop variant is worse: an entire fabric silently vanishes from the order BOM and is never procured.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED IN CODE. backend/src/controllers/styleCosting.controller.ts:1068-1070 is exactly as claimed: `const idx = fabricItemsToCreate.length; const jsonFabric = fabricDetails[idx]; if (!jsonFabric) continue;` — a raw positional join between fabric_width_cad rows read with `orderBy: { updatedAt: 'desc' }` (line 1055) and the frontend's fabricDetails JSON array. Lines 1082-1092 confirm the split the claim describes: identity columns (fabricCADId, fabricId, greigeId, width) come from the CAD row while money columns (fabricName, cadMeters, costPerMeter, totalCost) come from the JSON entry, so a mispair yields an internally inconsistent row. The create path (lines 299-359) genuinely does try fabricId -> greigeId -> fabricName before falling back to index WITH a console.warn; the update path has no matching and no warning at all. Not baselined: scripts/hooks/*-baseline.json only carry unrelated `?? 10.0` buffer-percent entries for this file.

REACHABLE, WITH LIVE CORRUPT DATA. Live DB: 21 styles (not "30+") have >1 unique CAD key (componentName|style_fabric_id|cutableWidth); 730c69e4 has 4 and six styles have 3. Twelve cost sheets currently hold >=2 style_costing_fabric_items, and 5 of those have been saved again after creation, so the update path is exercised on multi-fabric sheets. I found one genuinely cross-paired sheet, CS-1787201065404-j5whprg (style 7b69fb43, PENDING): CAD 84dc0efb is the Nazneen row (width 40, cadAverage 2.35, totalCostPerMeter 26) but its item reads fabricName "Viscose Shantoon", cadMeters 3.3, costPerMeter 77, totalCost 254.10; CAD 449a4645 is the Viscose Shantoon row (width 52, cadAverage 3.3, rate 77) but its item reads "Nazneen", 2.35m @ 26 = 61.10. width tracks the CAD row while the meters/rate track the other fabric — precisely the internal inconsistency predicted. The sheet total (315.20) is unchanged, which is why nobody noticed; the damage is in the per-fabric BOM/MRP/procurement lines, where Nazneen is priced at a ~3x rate and Shantoon is under-metered. Corroborating the instability argument: that same style is the ONLY one in the DB where two distinct unique-key CAD rows share updatedAt to the millisecond (2026-08-20T04:45:58.414Z), so `orderBy: { updatedAt: 'desc' }` has literally no tiebreaker there.

WHERE THE CLAIM IS WRONG — THE BLAME IS MISATTRIBUTED. The corrupt sheet has createdAt === updatedAt (2026-08-20T04:44:28.374Z); it was never updated. That crossing was written by the CREATE path. The reason matters: create's "P1.9 ID-based matching" is inert on real data. Every fabric_width_cad row for that style has fabricId = NULL, the stored fabricDetails entries carry no fabricId key at all (only fabricName/fabricAverage/fabricRate/fabricWidth), and the names never match — JSON "Nazneen" vs master `Nazneen 1x1 / 1x1 / 48" (Super Dyeing)`. So all three ID/name tiers miss and create falls to its index fallback, which assigns the first *unused* JSON fabric in the same CAD iteration order — i.e. the identical positional pairing. In production data the only practical difference between the two paths is a console.warn. Fixing only the update path would therefore NOT fix the observed corruption.

ALSO OVERSTATED. (a) The predicted flip-on-re-save has not fired anywhere: I replayed the update algorithm against all 12 multi-item sheets; 11 reproduce their stored values exactly. The single sheet that would change, CS-1786001599892-xnpp7ny, is not a swap (its two items have fabricCADId = NULL and would simply rebind) and it is APPROVED, so both the frontend (CostSheetForm.tsx:180) and the backend (styleCosting.controller.ts:869-873, BusinessError "Cannot update approved cost sheet") refuse the edit. The "re-cost the lining and the shell's money moves" scenario is a sound mechanism with zero live instances today. (b) The secondary point — `if (!jsonFabric) continue` never advances idx so trailing CAD rows are silently dropped — is true (two sheets show uniqCAD=3 vs json=2, one CAD silently itemless) but it is NOT an asymmetry: the create path does the same thing at line 359 once every JSON fabric is used. It is not a regression the update path introduced.

VERDICT: real, unguarded, unbaselined, silent, and demonstrably producing wrong per-fabric money in the live DB — worth fixing at major. But it is a shared create+update defect, not an update-path-only regression, and the fix must cover both.
verdict.fix:
Do not just port the create path's matcher into the update path — on live data that matcher never matches (CAD fabricId is NULL and JSON fabricNames are short names that never equal the master's descriptive name), so it degrades to the same positional join that already crossed CS-1787201065404-j5whprg.

1. Make the pairing explicit instead of heuristic. Persist the CAD row's id into each fabricDetails JSON entry at create time (add `fabricCADId` to FabricDetailSchema and have CostSheetForm.tsx carry it through, including the costing-run load at line 1789), then in BOTH styleCosting.controller.ts:308 (create) and :1061 (update) join on `jsonFabric.fabricCADId === cad.id`. That removes the ordering dependency entirely.

2. Until that lands, at minimum make the ordering deterministic — `orderBy: [{ updatedAt: 'desc' }, { id: 'asc' }]` at lines 1055 and 293 — so tied timestamps (which exist on style 7b69fb43) cannot reorder arbitrarily between runs.

3. Make the fallback loud, not silent. When a CAD row cannot be matched by id, the update path should refuse the save (or return a warning in the response) rather than writing a row whose width comes from one fabric and whose rate comes from another. Same for the trailing-CAD drop: if uniqueCADs > fabricDetails.length, surface "N CAD rows have no cost line" instead of silently skipping.

4. Data repair: CS-1787201065404-j5whprg needs its two style_costing_fabric_items swapped back (CAD 84dc0efb -> Nazneen 2.35m @ 26; CAD 449a4645 -> Viscose Shantoon 3.3m @ 77). Add a sweep in the style of scripts/check-phantom-approved-costings.ts that flags any style_costing_fabric_items row whose fabricCADId's CAD cadAverage/totalCostPerMeter disagree with the item's cadMeters/costPerMeter.

title: Editing an order's items destroys its frozen costing baseline; the re-snapshot runs outside the transaction and its failures are only logged
claim: State (verified live): ORD2026080030 (style ESSKY091LS) carries order_item_costing.costingSnapshot frozen at cost sheet v1 = Rs.225.42/pc, original_cost_sheet_version=1. ESSKY091LS now has approved v2 = Rs.224.00 (v1 is superseded). Input: user cancels the order's BOM/MRP (the guard at order.controller.ts:844 literally instructs 'Cancel the BOM/MRP first, then edit the order'), edits the size breakdown, saves. What is lost: the transaction at lines 891-956 runs tx.order_items.deleteMany (line 896), which CASCADE-deletes order_item_costing (schema.prisma:4844 onDelete: Cascade) - the v1 snapshot JSON is destroyed. The transaction then COMMITS. Only afterwards, OUTSIDE any transaction, line 961 calls createCostingSnapshots, which re-reads style_costing.findFirst({isApproved:true, supersededById:null}) and writes v2 (Rs.224.00) in its place. The order's frozen price silently rebases to a sheet approved after it was placed. If the style has no live approved sheet at all, order.service.ts:383 pushes 'No approved cost sheet found for style' into failures and the order is left with NO order_item_costing row at all - no variance anchor, no originalCostSheetVersion, no estimatedCostPerPiece - and there is no rollback because the destroying transaction already committed. Why it is silent: line 964-969 only logWarn the failures; the response at line 1015 is {data: order, message: 'Order updated successfully'} with no failures key. The sibling createOrder path calls the identical helper and DOES surface them (order.controller.ts:318, `failures: costingFailures.length > 0 ? costingFailures : undefined`), proving the channel exists and was simply not wired here. The third caller, order.service.ts:263 (createWithItems, the Sale Order -> startProduction path), has the same silent logWarn-only handling.
userImpact: An order's agreed cost basis is rewritten to a newer price, or erased entirely, by an ordinary edit. Cost-variance reporting then compares actuals against a baseline that was never the one the order was sold on, or against nothing. This directly violates the project's own 'rates freeze at costing qty, never re-derive downstream' invariant, and the loss is irreversible because the superseded snapshot JSON is the only record of the original rates.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED as a real silent-data-loss defect, but "critical" is overstated — downgraded to major.

EVERY LINK VERIFIED IN THE CURRENT TREE:
1. `backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts:896` — `tx.order_items.deleteMany({ where: { orderId: id } })` inside the `$transaction` at :891-956.
2. `backend/prisma/schema.prisma:4844` — `order_item @relation(fields: [orderItemId], ... onDelete: Cascade)` on `order_item_costing`. The delete destroys `costing_snapshot`, `original_cost_sheet_version`, `estimated_cost_per_piece`, `baseCostingId`.
3. The transaction COMMITS at :956. The re-snapshot at :961 (`orderService.createCostingSnapshots`) runs after, outside any tx — exactly as claimed.
4. `backend/src/services/order.service.ts:373-380` — the helper re-reads `style_costing.findFirst({ isApproved: true, supersededById: null }, orderBy: { version: 'desc' })`, i.e. whatever is approved NOW, and writes `originalCostSheetVersion: costSheet.version` (:433). Nothing carries the pre-delete version forward.
5. `order.service.ts:382-388` — the no-sheet branch pushes 'No approved cost sheet found for style' into `failures` and `continue`s, leaving the item with no `order_item_costing` row at all.
6. SILENCE CONFIRMED: `order.controller.ts:964-969` is `logWarn` only; the response at :1013-1016 is `{ data, message: 'Order updated successfully' }` with no failures key. The sibling `createOrder` at :318 does emit `failures`.

REACHABILITY FROM THE REAL UI (this is what makes it real, not theoretical):
`frontend/src/pages/OrderForm.tsx:1036-1046` sends `orderData.items` on edit precisely when `!hasDownstreamDeps` — i.e. exactly after the user does what the backend guard at order.controller.ts:844 tells them to do ("Cancel the BOM/MRP first, then edit the order"). `updateOrderSchema = createOrderSchema.partial()` (order.schema.ts:56) permits `items` on PUT, so nothing strips it. On success OrderForm.tsx:1050 just `navigate('/orders')` — no message at all.

LIVE DB CONFIRMS THE SCENARIO'S PREMISE (read-only queries):
- ORD2026080030 / ESSKY091LS: status PENDING, `original_cost_sheet_version=1`, `estimated_cost_per_piece=225.42`, snapshot 2026-08-25T08:58.
- ESSKY091LS style_costing: v1 isApproved, supersededById='CS-1787665155067-lrf8yvx', 225.42; v2 isApproved, supersededById NULL, 224.00, approved 2026-08-25T13:39 — i.e. approved AFTER the order's snapshot. Re-snapshot would pick v2 and silently rebase the anchor 225.42 -> 224.00.
- Of 8 PENDING orders, ORD2026080030 is the only one whose snap_ver (1) differs from live_ver (2).

WHY I DOWNGRADED TO MAJOR:
- Zero rows are corrupted today. ORD2026080030 currently has 2 APPROVED BOMs + 8 active material_requirements, so the guard blocks the edit right now; it is one deliberate BOM/MRP cancellation away. The only order editable today (ORD2026080032) has snap_ver == live_ver == 1, so nothing would change.
- What corrupts is the internal costing baseline / variance anchor (consumed by manufacturing-alerts.service.ts:427 and fg-stock.controller.ts:136-144), NOT the customer-facing order price/quantity, which come from the payload and are recomputed correctly.
- The "left with NO order_item_costing at all" sub-branch is largely guarded in practice, contrary to the claim's framing: OrderForm.tsx:971 + 1005-1016 refuse to Save unless `hasApprovedCostSheet === true`, and `getCostSheetOrderDependents` (cad-costing-provenance.helper.ts:271-278) 409-blocks COST_SHEET_IN_USE on revoke/reject/edit/delete for any sheet referenced by a non-CANCELLED order's `baseCostingId`. There are also zero multi-style orders live, closing the passthrough-item hole. That branch is realistically API-only, not UI-reachable.
- The claim's "proving the channel exists" is half-true: `costingInfo.failures` is returned by createOrder, but grep shows the frontend never reads `costingInfo` anywhere — so it is an API-level channel only, not something the user sees today.

TWO THINGS THE CLAIM UNDER-STATES (they strengthen it):
- The recreated row also drops fields `createCostingSnapshots` never writes (order.service.ts:418-437): `selectedCadId`, `cadMeters`, `cadWidth`, `processingTotal`, `overheadsTotal`, `actualCostPerPiece`, `costVariance*`, `recalculatedAt`. The order-specific CAD choice written by `orderCosting.service.ts:220-257` / `selectCadAndRecalculate` is silently reset to null. Currently structural only — a live count shows all 8 rows have selectedCadId/actual/variance NULL.
- After the rebase, `baseCostingId` moves v1 -> v2, which releases v1 from the COST_SHEET_IN_USE guard, so the sheet the order was actually quoted against becomes editable/deletable.

Not baselined: I checked scripts/hooks/*-baseline.json concerns — this is not a `|| fallback` or schema-alignment entry, and no smart-check covers post-transaction re-snapshot or cascade-through-costing. The author was aware of the cascade (comment at order.controller.ts:779 "cascading order_item_costing etc.") but the mitigation preserved neither the version nor the failure signal.
verdict.fix:
Three changes in `backend/src/controllers/order.controller.ts` updateOrder:

1. PRESERVE THE ORIGINAL BASELINE. Before the `$transaction` at :891, read the existing rows keyed by styleId:
   const priorCosting = await prisma.order_item_costing.findMany({ where: { order_item: { orderId: id } }, include: { order_item: { select: { styleId: true } } } });
   After recreating items, re-write each new item's costing from the prior row for the same styleId — keeping `baseCostingId`, `costingSnapshot`, `originalCostSheetVersion`, `snapshotCreatedAt`, `selectedCadId`, `cadMeters`, `cadWidth`, `processingTotal`, `overheadsTotal`, `actualCostPerPiece`, `costVariance*`. Only fall back to `createCostingSnapshots` for a styleId that had no prior row (a genuinely new style on the order). `originalCostSheetVersion` means "the version this order was placed against"; an item-quantity edit must not rebase it onto a sheet approved later.

2. MOVE IT INSIDE THE TRANSACTION. Give `createCostingSnapshots` an optional `tx` parameter (it already uses `this.prisma` at order.service.ts:373 and :418) and call it inside the `$transaction` block, so a failed re-snapshot rolls the item replacement back instead of committing an order with a destroyed baseline.

3. SURFACE THE FAILURES. Mirror createOrder (order.controller.ts:318) in the PUT response at :1013:
   res.json({ data: order, message: 'Order updated successfully', costingInfo: resnapshot.failures.length > 0 ? { failures: resnapshot.failures } : undefined });
   and have `frontend/src/pages/OrderForm.tsx` (around :1049) show the returned failures instead of navigating away silently — it currently ignores `costingInfo` on both the create and update paths.

Optional guardrail (matches the repo's smart-check pattern): flag any post-`$transaction` write that repairs state the transaction cascade-deleted.

title: Cancelling a partially-received PO silently strands its material requirements, making the un-received remainder permanently un-orderable
claim: Input/state: a PO is raised from MRP (its material_requirements go to PO_GENERATED), a GRN arrives for part of it, so mrp.service.ts:4348 moves those requirements to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED and the PO to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. The supplier then defaults on the balance and the user cancels the PO - the state machine explicitly permits this (stateMachine.ts:48, PARTIALLY_RECEIVED: ['RECEIVED','CANCELLED']). What is lost: cancelPurchaseOrder's revert at line 903 is `updateMany({ where: { id: { in: ... }, status: 'PO_GENERATED' }, data: { status: 'PO_REQUIRED' } })`. The requirements are in PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, so the where-clause matches ZERO rows. The same hole exists for PO_SENT, which mrp.service.ts:4353 sets on a full GRN reversal, and which stateMachine.ts:113 explicitly lists as revertible to PO_REQUIRED. The requirements stay pinned to a CANCELLED PO forever. They can never be re-ordered: generatePOFromRequirements only accepts PO_REQUIRED/PARTIAL_STOCK (mrp.service.ts:3936), and the duplicate guard at mrp.service.ts:2057 explicitly skips anything in PO_GENERATED/PO_SENT/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED. The MRP 'needing PO' tile counts only PO_REQUIRED/PARTIAL_STOCK (mrp.service.ts:2613-2619), so the shortfall vanishes from the procurement screen. Why it is silent: updateMany returns {count: 0}, which is indistinguishable from success because the result is never assigned or checked, and no exception is raised. The controller responds 'Purchase order cancelled successfully' (purchaseOrder.controller.ts:363). The codebase already knows the correct pattern in both respects: mrp.service.ts:3937 performs the same guarded flip and THROWS when flipResult.count != expected, and job-work-order.controller.ts:1300 reverts with status: { in: ['PO_GENERATED','PO_SENT'] }. Only this PO-cancel path does neither. (DB check: 0 cancelled POs today, so no rows are corrupted yet - the defect is reachable but has not fired.)

title: Purchase Order edit: delivery location renders blank then is dropped, and item fold lengths are wiped
claim: Two distinct losses on PO edit. (`item.foldLengthCm` is already on the serialized item type, purchaseOrder.types.ts:391, and the update Zod item schema already accepts it, purchaseOrder.schema.ts:68 — so no backend change is needed.) Optionally, since `purchase_order_items.foldLengthCm` currently has no reader anywhere, the cheaper alternative is to drop the "L" column from the PO form entirely and let the GRN own fold length, which is where it is actually consumed.

(2) Delivery location: stop the edit form from offering a control whose value is thrown away. Either
  (a) prefill it and make it read-only in edit mode — add `if (po.deliveryLocationId) setDeliveryLocationId(po.deliveryLocationId);` in `fetchPurchaseOrder` and render the combobox disabled with a link/hint pointing at the audited "Amend Delivery Location" action on the PO detail page (PATCH /purchase-orders/:id/delivery-location); or

The code chain is real and I traced every link, but the claim is overstated on impact and on its DB evidence, so I am confirming it at reduced severity.

So the residual defect is a blank prefill plus a dead combobox — a UI wiring gap, not procurement data loss.

WHERE THE CLAIM'S EVIDENCE FAILS:
- "All 6 live purchase_order_items rows currently carry a foldLengthCm, so the field is in real use" is a non-sequitur for reachability. Live DB query: all 6 rows do carry foldLengthCm (all = 100), but every one of their 6 POs is status='RECEIVED', which `updatePurchaseOrder` rejects ("Can only update purchase orders in Draft, Pending Greige, or Ready for Processing status"). ZERO live rows are at risk today; only future drafts are.
- `purchase_order_items.foldLengthCm` has NO reader anywhere in the repo. NET: real, silent, reachable — but it corrupts a write-only field with no consumer, hits no live row today, and its delivery-location half is a deliberate, already-baselined design. Downgrading major -> minor.

title: Cutting batch completion writes one batch's consumption onto every RESERVED allocation for the order, then silently records nothing for later batches
claim: Input/state: progressive cutting across lays is a first-class flow - cutting_batches.workOrderId has no unique constraint (schema.prisma:6201) and cutting.controller.ts:2182-2194 computes alreadyCutQty/pendingCutQty across existingBatches. Each batch creation calls fabric_stock_allocation.create (line 325) keyed ONLY by (stockId, orderId, styleId) with no batch reference and no unique constraint (schema.prisma:5092-5127). So two batches on the same order/style/roll produce two RESERVED allocation rows. What is lost: when batch 1 completes, line 896 runs `updateMany({ where: { stockId, orderId, styleId, allocationStatus: 'RESERVED' }, data: { allocationStatus: 'CONSUMED', quantityConsumed: actualConsumed, quantityReturned: returned, actualCad, consumptionDate } })`. This matches BOTH rows and ASSIGNS batch 1's consumption to each, so batch 2's untouched reservation is prematurely flipped to CONSUMED and stamped with a quantity that was never cut. When batch 2 later completes, the same updateMany finds no RESERVED rows and matches zero - batch 2's real consumption is never recorded in the allocation ledger at all. fabric-stock.service.ts:355 aggregates _sum.quantityConsumed per style to produce the 'stockConsumed' figure on the Fabric-usage-by-style view, which is therefore wrong in both directions. Why it is silent: the updateMany result is never assigned, so count=0 looks exactly like success; no exception is thrown, so the wrapping catch at line 913 never fires; and that catch is marked `// allow-swallow` (line 914), deliberately opting the block out of the repo's swallowed-write guardrail. The batch itself reports success with a correct actualConsumption on cutting_batches, so the UI looks right while the allocation ledger diverges.
userImpact: Fabric consumption per style is double-counted for the first cut and dropped entirely for every subsequent one, so fabric-usage and CAD-variance reporting are wrong, and stock stays flagged as reserved-then-consumed against quantities that were never actually cut.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED as a real, unguarded correctness defect, but DOWNGRADED from major to minor: the corruption reaches only informational report columns, and the subsystem has zero rows in the live DB.

Every cited link verified in the current tree:
- schema.prisma:5092-5128 — fabric_stock_allocation has NO batch/workOrder column and NO unique constraint on (stockId, orderId, styleId); only plain @@index entries. Confirmed.
- cutting.controller.ts:325 — creates a RESERVED row keyed solely by (stockId, orderId, styleId), unconditionally, with no lookup for an existing reservation. Guard is only `cadAvg > 0 && totalPiecesToCut > 0 && workOrder.orderId`; cadAverageUsed is mandatory and >0 (controller line 228, production.schema.ts:70) and skuOutputs is .min(1), so every batch on an order-linked WO creates a row.
- cutting.controller.ts:896 — unbounded updateMany on that same key + allocationStatus:'RESERVED', ASSIGNING (not incrementing) this batch's quantityConsumed/quantityReturned/actualCad to every match. Confirmed verbatim.
- Silence confirmed: the updateMany result is discarded, a 0-count match is not an error, and the wrapping catch at 913-918 carries `// allow-swallow`. Not baselined — I checked all 25 scripts/hooks/*-baseline.json; neither "cutting.controller" nor "fabric_stock_allocation" appears in swallowed-write-baseline.json or silent-catch-baseline.json. The inline allow-swallow marker exempts the catch, not the updateMany fan-out.

REACHABILITY IS STRONGER THAN THE CLAIM ARGUED. The claim leans on two concurrently-open progressive batches, which is plausible (no guard in createCuttingBatch prevents multiple open batches per WO, and the cutting chart at 2180-2192 explicitly models alreadyCut/pendingCut across batches) but unproven. There is a strictly sequential single-operator path that needs no concurrency: cancelCuttingBatch (1137-1192) restores fabric stock and sets status ON_HOLD but NEVER touches the allocation, and deleteCuttingBatch (502-566) deletes the batch while the allocation — having no FK to it — survives as an orphan RESERVED row. Cancel or delete batch A, create batch B on the same roll, complete B: the updateMany stamps B's consumption onto A's dead reservation as well, double-counting it. Also, a single create can produce two identical rows: allStocksToReserve (314-320) filters only against the primary fabricStockId and does not dedupe fabricStocks against itself, while cutting_batch_fabrics.createMany uses skipDuplicates — CuttingChart.tsx:197 flatMaps selected lots across fabric PARTS, so two parts sharing one lot yield a duplicate entry.

WHERE THE CLAIM OVERREACHES (basis for the downgrade):
1. Blast radius. fabric_stock_allocation is written only by these two sites and read by exactly three: fabric-stock.service.ts:355 groupBy -> stockAllocated/stockConsumed rendered at FabricUsageReport.tsx:246,249; the allocation list on the stock-detail page (fabric-stock.controller.ts:587-627); and a status-independent delete-dependency count (line 1298). The cad-planning.controller.ts:3922 read filters productionCadId:{not:null}, which the cutting path never sets, so these rows never surface there. Nothing here drives fabric_stock.quantityAvailable/quantityConsumed (owned by challan.service.ts:326/355/418), MRP, procurement, costing, or any priced document. So the damage is two report columns plus a ledger list — not the stock balance, not money, not a procurement/production document.
2. The claim's assertion that "the batch itself reports success with a correct actualConsumption, so the UI looks right" is wrong in the claim's own favor: issuedMap is built from challan_items grouped by fabricStockId where challan.productionRunId = workOrderId (lines 740-761) — work-order-scoped, not batch-scoped — so on a multi-batch WO each batch's fabricIssued/actualConsumption/wastageMeters/variancePercent is already cumulative across the whole WO. That is a separate (and arguably larger) defect in the same handler.
3. Zero live incidence. Read-only queries against garment_erp (current_database confirmed): fabric_stock_allocation 0 rows, cutting_batches 0, cutting_batch_fabrics 0, work_orders 0, fabric_stock 0, production_tracking 0 (orders 8, challans 3). The entire cutting/allocation subsystem has never been exercised, so no data is corrupted today and no user has yet seen a wrong number from it. This is a latent defect on an unused path, which is why it is minor rather than major — it would become materially worse the day the cutting module goes live.
verdict.fix:
Give the allocation a batch identity and scope the write to it.

1. Schema: add `cuttingBatchId String?` (with an index, and ideally `@@unique([cuttingBatchId, stockId])`) to `fabric_stock_allocation` in backend/prisma/schema.prisma:5092.
2. backend/src/controllers/cutting.controller.ts:325 — set `cuttingBatchId: batch.id` on the create, and dedupe `allStocksToReserve` (lines 310-320) by stockId before the loop so one batch can never emit two rows for the same roll.
3. backend/src/controllers/cutting.controller.ts:896 — change the where clause from `{ stockId, orderId, styleId, allocationStatus:'RESERVED' }` to `{ cuttingBatchId: existing.id, stockId }`, turning the fan-out into a 1:1 update. title: Purchase-order edit orphans MRP-to-PO links and strands requirements at PO_GENERATED forever (GRN half REFUTED)
claim: updatePurchaseOrder accepts POs in DRAFT, PENDING_GREIGE and READY_FOR_PROCESSING (lines 346-362). When `data.items` is supplied it collects the PO's existing item ids and, before replacing them, executes `tx.requirement_po_links.deleteMany({ where: { purchaseOrderItemId: { in: itemIds } } })` (line 425) and `tx.grn_items.deleteMany({ where: { poItemId: { in: itemIds } } })` (line 428), then deletes the items (line 434) and creates fresh ones with `receivedQuantity: 0` hardcoded (line 475). Nothing in the remainder of the transaction (lines 438-517, which only recreate purchase_order_items and recompute GST/header totals) recreates the requirement links or the GRN lines, and no material_requirements status is reverted. This is a deliberate-looking "clean up linked records" that is actually an unrecoverable delete of receipt and planning history. The same file's deletePurchaseOrder (line 526) and the JWO cancel path (controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:1289-1305) both show the correct pattern — the JWO path reverts material_requirements back to PO_REQUIRED in the same breath as deleting requirement_jwo_links, and refuses to revert links whose receivedQuantity is non-zero. updatePurchaseOrder does neither check. READY_FOR_PROCESSING is not a draft state: services/po-status-manager.service.ts flips a processing PO from PENDING_GREIGE to READY_FOR_PROCESSING after the greige GRN lands and quantities are reconciled, so an edit there operates on a PO with real upstream history. Currently latent in this database (all 6 POs are RECEIVED and requirement_po_links is empty), so this is reachable-by-design rather than already-fired.
userImpact: Editing a live greige/processing PO destroys the audit trail of what was physically received against it (grn_items) while the stock those GRNs created stays on hand — the GRN reads as empty, so receipts can be booked twice and supplier reconciliation silently breaks. Separately, the MRP requirements that the PO was covering keep their PO_GENERATED/PO_SENT status but lose the requirement_po_links row that points at the PO, so they render as "covered by a PO" on the MRP page with no PO behind them: they are never re-proposed for procurement and the material is never bought. Resetting receivedQuantity to 0 on every recreated line compounds it, making a partially-received PO look untouched. The user sees a successful save.

verdict.reasoning:
PARTLY CONFIRMED. The MRP-link half is a real, reachable, silent, non-self-healing data-loss bug. The GRN half is REFUTED as unreachable, and the reporter's mechanism is mis-attributed.

1) CODE EXISTS AS CLAIMED. backend/src/services/purchaseOrder.service.ts: editableStatuses = DRAFT, PENDING_GREIGE, READY_FOR_PROCESSING (346-350), enforced at 360-362. Inside the tx: `await tx.requirement_po_links.deleteMany({ where: { purchaseOrderItemId: { in: itemIds } } })` (425-427); `await tx.grn_items.deleteMany({ where: { poItemId: { in: itemIds } } })` (428-430); `tx.purchase_order_items.deleteMany({ where: { poId: id } })` (434-436); recreate with `receivedQuantity: 0` (475). I read to the end of the function (517/519): after recreate there is ONLY the GST/header recompute (496-508) and a re-fetch (513-515). Nothing recreates links or GRN lines; no material_requirements revert. The controller (purchaseOrder.controller.ts:192-209) adds no guard, and the route (purchaseOrder.routes.ts:127-132) has validateParams/validateBody but NO `authorize` — only authenticateToken.

2) MECHANISM IS MIS-ATTRIBUTED (refutes the reporter's framing). All four children of purchase_order_items are `onDelete: Cascade` in schema.prisma: requirement_po_links.purchaseOrderItemId, grn_items.poItemId, po_source_links.purchaseOrderItemId, service_requirement_po_links.purchaseOrderItemId. The deleteMany at 425/428 is REDUNDANT — line 434 destroys those rows via DB cascade regardless. Deleting the two deleteMany lines would fix nothing. Conversely the bug is BROADER than reported: po_source_links (the newer unified link table written by unified-po-creation.service.ts:589) and service_requirement_po_links also vanish and aren't even mentioned in the cleanup.

3) GRN HALF REFUTED — UNREACHABLE. A grn_item only gets a non-null poItemId from ONE site, grn.service.ts:183-197 (createGRN), gated at 92-98 by receivableStatuses = SENT, ACKNOWLEDGED, PARTIALLY_RECEIVED. The only other GRN creator, createGRNFromJWO (grn.service.ts:2586, create at 2689), writes `poId: null` / `poItemId: null`. After receipt updateReceivingStatus (purchaseOrder.service.ts:937-968) lands on RECEIVED / PARTIALLY_RECEIVED, or ACKNOWLEDGED on full QC rejection (959-960); reverseGRN also lands on ACKNOWLEDGED (grn.service.ts:3621-3622). I enumerated every purchase_orders status write: nothing ever writes a PO back to DRAFT or PENDING_GREIGE, and READY_FOR_PROCESSING is written only by po-status-manager.service.ts:161-164 from `status: 'PENDING_GREIGE'` (121-125) — a PO that by construction never had a GRN (the GRN belongs to the LINKED GREIGE PO, not the processing PO). So no PO can hold grn_items while in an editable status. The claimed impact "destroys the audit trail of what was physically received... receipts can be double-booked" is FALSE. For the same reason `receivedQuantity: 0` at 475 is harmless: an editable PO always already has 0 received.

4) MRP-LINK HALF CONFIRMED AND REACHABLE. mrp.service.ts:3852 `const initialStatus = PurchaseOrderStatus.DRAFT` — generatePOFromRequirements (3122) creates the PO as DRAFT, creates requirement_po_links (4002-4009) and flips material_requirements to PO_GENERATED. Live and wired: POST /api/mrp/generate-po and /generate-pos-bulk (mrp.routes.ts:184-187, 213). Frontend: PurchaseOrderList.tsx:622 exposes Edit for `po.status === 'DRAFT'`; PurchaseOrderDetail.tsx:288 `canEdit = ['DRAFT','PENDING_GREIGE','READY_FOR_PROCESSING']`. PurchaseOrderForm.tsx:983-989 ALWAYS sends `items: itemsData` on edit — so the delete/recreate path runs on every UI edit. No guard blocks it anywhere.

5) CONSEQUENCE CONFIRMED, NO SELF-HEAL. The requirement is left at PO_GENERATED with zero links. Every PO-candidate query allowlists PO_REQUIRED/PARTIAL_STOCK (mrp.service.ts:2619, 2708 raw SQL, 3188, 3658, 3935), so the orphan is never re-proposed and the material is never bought. The only repair tool, backend/scripts/recompute-requirement-statuses.ts, explicitly declines this exact state: `if (links.length === 0) { // No links but has PO status — might be a bug, but leave it alone; continue; }`. It is manual-only (no scheduler reference). Contrast confirmed at controllers/job-work-order.controller.ts:1276-1307 — the JWO cancel path reverts PO_GENERATED/PO_SENT → PO_REQUIRED and only unlinks rows with receivedQuantity === 0.

6) LIVE DB — LATENT, HAS NOT FIRED. purchase_orders: 6 total, all RECEIVED, all poSource MANUAL. POs in DRAFT/PENDING_GREIGE/READY_FOR_PROCESSING: 0. requirement_po_links: 0 rows (the MRP→PO flow has never been used here). grn_items: 6, all on RECEIVED POs. material_requirements: 91 (46 PO_REQUIRED, 38 CANCELLED, 4 SIZE_PENDING, 2 FULFILLED_STOCK, 1 PARTIAL_STOCK) — zero in PO_GENERATED/PO_SENT, so zero orphans. Nothing is at risk right now.

SEVERITY: major, not critical. Downgraded from the reporter's implied blast radius because the stock/receipt-corruption half is impossible and no data is currently exposed. Kept at major rather than minor because the surviving half is silent, permanent (explicitly skipped by the only repair script), triggered by an entirely ordinary action — "MRP generated the DRAFT PO, let me fix a quantity before sending" — and the loss is business-visible only much later as material that was never purchased.
verdict.reasoning_second_lens:
CONFIRMED, but the claim is HALF right on impact: the MRP-link half is real and reachable in one click; the GRN-audit-trail half is unreachable and overstated. The finding also UNDERSTATES the blast radius in two ways it never mentions.

1. THE CODE EXISTS, VERBATIM. backend/src/services/purchaseOrder.service.ts, inside updatePurchaseOrder, gated only by `if (data.items)` (line 417) and `itemIds.length > 0` (424):

  427  });
  428  await tx.grn_items.deleteMany({

  434  await tx.purchase_order_items.deleteMany({ where: { poId: id } });

Editable statuses at 346-350 = DRAFT, PENDING_GREIGE, READY_FOR_PROCESSING (guard at 360-362). Line numbers in the claim are accurate.

2. NOTHING IS RECREATED OR COMPENSATED. I read the function to its end (400-519): after the delete it only recreates purchase_order_items with fresh randomUUID()s (467-491) and rewrites GST/header totals (496-508), then re-reads the PO. The controller (purchaseOrder.controller.ts:192-209) just logs and returns 200. No other backend caller — the sole entry is PUT /api/purchase-orders/:id (purchaseOrder.routes.ts:127-132), which carries validateBody but NO `authorize()` despite its "(PURCHASE, ADMIN)" doc comment, so any authenticated user reaches it. No repair script rebuilds links (backend/scripts has no such sweep).

3. REACHABILITY OF THE LINK HALF: REACHABLE TODAY, BY DESIGN, ONE CLICK.

4. FK REALITY MAKES IT WORSE THAN CLAIMED (live pg_constraint check on purchase_order_items): grn_items, requirement_po_links, po_source_links and service_requirement_po_links are ALL ON DELETE CASCADE ('c'); order_thread_requirements is SET NULL ('n'). So (a) both explicit deleteManys are redundant — line 434 destroys those rows anyway; (b) nothing aborts the transaction; (c) two tables the claim never mentions die silently: po_source_links (the modern provenance table that powers unified-po-creation's cross-source duplicate detection) and service_requirement_po_links; (d) order_thread_requirements.poItemId is nulled while the row stays PO_GENERATED (order-thread-requirement.service.ts:697-706), an identical strand for thread procurement.

5. CONSEQUENCE OF LOSING THE LINK — PERMANENT, SILENT, AND WORSE THAN "NEVER RE-PROPOSED":
 - cancelPurchaseOrder (:898-910) reverts requirements by joining through requirement_po_links. Links gone → zero rows matched → requirement stays PO_GENERATED forever.
 - mrp.service.updateReceivedQuantity (:4295) finds no links → the requirement never advances to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED even when the goods physically arrive.
 - Re-planning cannot rescue it: the recalc supersede-cancel excludes PO_GENERATED (:1151) so the row is never cancelled, and the rebuild skip-probe (:2040-2057) keys on status alone — PO_GENERATED means "already has an active PO", so it is skipped on every recalculation. Fresh PO generation is also closed: :3188 and :3935 accept only PO_REQUIRED/PARTIAL_STOCK.
 - The UI offers no escape: UnifiedRequirementsPage.tsx:1069/1264 make only PO_REQUIRED/PARTIAL_STOCK selectable, and :1197/:1400 render Cancel only for PENDING/PO_REQUIRED. A PO_GENERATED orphan has literally no action.

With the link destroyed it falls to :1082 `logWarn('No requirement linked to PROCESSING PO - cannot create fabric_stock')` — the GRN approves, the PO goes RECEIVED, and NO fabric_stock row is ever created. THE grn_items HALF IS OVERSTATED — IT IS UNREACHABLE. grn.service.ts:92-100 admits a GRN only for SENT/ACKNOWLEDGED/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED; a receipt then drives the PO to PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED (purchaseOrder.service.ts:945-968); the only downgrade is → ACKNOWLEDGED (:958-961), still not editable; stateMachine.ts:45-54 has no transition back to DRAFT/PENDING_GREIGE/READY_FOR_PROCESSING; shadow-po.helper.ts never regresses a PO either; reverseGRN keeps its grn_items and only recomputes via that same path; and JWO-sourced GRNs write poItemId: null (grn.service.ts:2710) so they are untouched. Therefore no PO in an editable status can carry grn_items, and the claimed "receipts double-booked / stock on hand with no GRN line / supplier reconciliation destroyed" cannot occur today. Same for point 4 of the brief: `receivedQuantity: 0` at line 475 is genuinely hardcoded, but nothing already posted can be corrupted by it — no editable-status PO can have receivedQuantity > 0 (verified: 0 rows). Both are latent traps that go live the moment anyone widens editableStatuses or adds a receipt-then-reopen path, not live defects.

7. LIVE DB (read-only, garment_erp): 6 purchase_orders TOTAL, all status RECEIVED, all poSource MANUAL / poCategory GREIGE. ZERO in DRAFT/PENDING_GREIGE/READY_FOR_PROCESSING. requirement_po_links = 0 rows; po_source_links = 0; service_requirement_po_links = 0. grn_items = 6, all 6 carrying a poItemId, all on RECEIVED (non-editable) POs. material_requirements: 46 PO_REQUIRED, 38 CANCELLED, 4 SIZE_PENDING, 2 FULFILLED_STOCK, 1 PARTIAL_STOCK — ZERO in PO_GENERATED/PO_SENT/PARTIALLY_RECEIVED/RECEIVED, hence zero orphans. No PO item with receivedQuantity > 0 on an editable PO. PLAINLY: this has NOT fired. MRP-driven PO generation has never completed in this installation (that is why the link tables are empty and all 6 POs are MANUAL), so the defect is fully LATENT — but it is not guarded, and the first MRP or processing PO raised makes it a one-click loss.

SEVERITY: major, not critical. It is a real, unguarded, permanently-damaging defect on a first-class flow, but nothing is corrupted today and it needs the MRP/processing-PO path to be used at all. This matches the calibration already set for the sibling finding in the same file (SILENT-DATA-LOSS-FINDINGS.json:180, cancelPurchaseOrder's silent no-op: confirmed, latent, kept at major).
